name: Canadian Cancer Society wig service
summary: Lends a wig at no charge to people who can't afford one. Request it through the online wig form, or call for help filling it in.
checkNote: The page could not be opened directly when this was checked; the details come from search excerpts of it. Confirm on the page before relying on them.

name: Tata Memorial Centre and The Cherian Foundation
summary: 500 wigs offered free to people in treatment who are economically disadvantaged, handed out through the Tata Memorial network from Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai (announced 19 August 2026).
checkNote: The number of wigs is limited and the article does not say how to apply. Ask your own Tata Memorial centre.

name: Cope With Cancer (Madat Charitable Trust)
summary: A Mumbai charity that offers free wigs to people in and after cancer treatment, alongside discounted care and free counselling.
checkNote: Described on a fundraising page; check their own website (copewithcancer.org) for how to apply.

name: The Christie, Manchester: free wig
summary: One free wig if your treatment causes hair loss. Ask at the hospital's cancer information centre for a voucher for the wig service.
checkNote: This is one hospital. Entitlement and voucher values differ between NHS trusts, so ask your own hospital's cancer information centre.

name: Macmillan Cancer Support helpline
summary: Information about wigs, hats and scalp care, every day from 8am to 8pm.
checkNote: Taken from a hospital page that quotes the helpline.

name: American Cancer Society helpline
summary: Can refer you to programmes and resources near you. Some hospitals and cancer centres run free wig banks, so ask about them.
checkNote: Wig banks vary by location and some listings are out of date. Call before you go.

name: Look Good Feel Better
summary: Free workshops, online and in person, with makeup, skincare and hair tips for people in treatment. Useful for practising brows. It does not provide wigs.
checkNote: Choose a workshop on their site.
